title: Author an affix template
description: Stages an active alternative template on an existing category, using ordered prefix and suffix slots that belong to the category or an ancestor. It preserves existing template order and records whether a word can end after this template. Only a person can Apply.
helpPage:
# Author an affix template

Use this command when two branches of a category need different required slots. It adds an active alternative template without changing the category's existing templates or their order.

```sh
motif compose-author-affix-template --project language.fwdata --draft plural-branch \
  --intent '{"category":"<category-id>","name":"plural branch","ws":"en","prefixSlots":["<prefix-slot-id>"],"suffixSlots":["<suffix-slot-id>"],"final":true}'
```

`category` names the existing category that owns the new template. `name` and `ws` give the localized name. `prefixSlots` and `suffixSlots` are ordered lists of existing slot ids from the project; each slot must belong to the template category or one of its ancestors. A slot may appear only once across both lists. The template is appended to the category's ordered template sequence.

`final` sets the template's Final value, which says whether a word can end after this template. Use `true` for a template that completes a word, which is the usual case and the value the project's other word-final templates have. Use `false` only for a template that a derivational affix continues from; a word cannot end after a `false` template, so with nothing continuing from it no word parses through it. The Dry Run warns when it finds a `false` template with no derivational affix that continues from its category. The template is active by default.

The Draft declares that the template create precedes its name, Final value and slot references. Finish the Proposal, inspect its Dry Run, and run a bounded Trial on affected words before a person Applies it.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on every operation this command produces.
